report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of session.py: council loop, budget/floor handling, helper functions; claims verified.
risks: line 1121-1126 | medium | Trusted lane on off-machine endpoint raises ValueError with repair message, but the message instructs to pass trusted_vendors, which is the explicit opt-in; however, the code does not check if the endpoint is actually off-machine; the check is based on lane only. Potential false positive for localhost endpoints with trusted lane. | Need to see the definition of _is_local_http and the condition that triggers this branch.

line 1150-1151 | medium | floor_check is called with evidence.paths and evidence.files, but the comment says 'Per path, per file, never over the assembled prompt'. The function signature is not visible; the claim that it never scans the assembled prompt is uncheckable from this chunk. | Need to see floor_check implementation.

line 1178-1179 | medium | The token ceiling check uses count_tokens(body) + evidence.text_tokens(). The comment says 'Charge the token ceiling BEFORE dispatch, from the assembled prompt. Reconciling after the call is not a budget.' This is consistent, but the actual token counting may not match the vendor's counting. Uncheckable. | Need to see count_tokens implementation and vendor token limits.

line 1204-1206 | medium | The timeout reason is inferred from presence of 'error' key in box. If a vendor returns an error object but also a reply, the reply is used; if no reply and no error, it's a timeout. The format of box is not pinned; uncheckable. | Need to see _dispatch_round return format.

line 1237-1239 | medium | The logic for updating outcomes: if ref.status is 'spoke' or 'anomaly', it sets outcome to 'responded' and increments spoke. If status is 'refused', it sets floor_rule if not already set. This may override a previously set floor_rule from a different actor. The comment says 'if ref.status == "refused" and not floor_rule' so it only sets if none. That is correct. No risk.

line 1255-1260 | medium | The participant_records construction uses outcomes dict; if an actor was over_budget and never got a turn, their outcome remains 'seated' from initialization. But _append_budget_round updates to 'unavailable' with reason 'budget_exhausted'. However, if the loop breaks due to wall_clock before _append_budget_round is called, actors may remain 'seated'. That is a potential inconsistency. | Need to see the wall_clock break handling: it calls _append_budget_round, so it's fine. If no_voice break, actors who didn't speak remain 'seated'? Actually they would have been updated in the loop for each turn; if they didn't speak, they might be 'refused' or 'unavailable' based on status. But if they were over_budget, they'd be 'unavailable' via _budget_turn. So it's consistent.
line 1288-1290 | medium | The chain verification uses verify_chain(store) and transcript_head(store). These functions are not defined in this chunk; uncheckable.

line 1305-1310 | medium | The CouncilRecord includes tokens_charged, token_ceiling, wall_clock_s. The wall_clock_s is rounded to 3 decimals. The claim that wall_clock_s is the actual elapsed time is kept. No risk.

handoff.purpose: Council execution loop: floor check, round dispatch, budget handling, outcome aggregation, and helper functions.

symbols.name: _first_offending_path
symbols.note: Returns the first evidence path whose secret_floor_rule fires, or empty string.

symbols.name: _unavailable_turn
symbols.note: Builds a turn dict with status 'unavailable' and given reason.

symbols.name: _append_budget_round
symbols.note: Appends a budget-exhausted round for all seated adapters and updates outcomes to unavailable with reason budget_exhausted.

symbols.name: _chained
symbols.note: Reads turns for a given round from the transcript store, filtering by record type 'turn' and round number.

symbols.name: _turn_ref
symbols.note: Constructs a TurnRef from a turn record, parsing fields and converting latency from ms to seconds.

claims.text: The operator say it out loud via ``trusted_vendors``.
claims.why: The ValueError message instructs to pass trusted_vendors explicitly, which is the opt-in mechanism.

claims.text: a trusted lane disables the egress allow-list and reports nothing withheld.
claims.why: The behavior of trusted lane is not fully defined in this chunk; the message states it, but the actual enforcement is elsewhere.

claims.text: PRE-FLIGHT SECRET FLOOR. Per path, per file, never over the assembled prompt: the path tier is the only thing that catches a patch which ADDS `.env`, and a concatenated scan kills it.
claims.why: The code calls floor_check with evidence paths and files, but the implementation of floor_check and whether it scans the assembled prompt is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: A hit refuses the whole council -- there is no redact-and-send -- and NO VENDOR IS CALLED.
claims.why: If refusal is not None, the code records a floor_refusal round and does not proceed to dispatch any jobs; no vendor calls are made.

claims.text: Charge the token ceiling BEFORE dispatch, from the assembled prompt. Reconciling after the call is not a budget.
claims.why: The code computes per_call_tokens = count_tokens(body) + evidence.text_tokens() and checks tokens_charged + per_call_tokens > token_ceiling before adding to jobs.

claims.text: Hung or crashed: recorded as a turn, never as an absence.
claims.why: If reply is None, it appends _unavailable_turn with reason 'timeout' or 'transport_error', which is a turn record.

claims.text: A blown budget is a RECORDED round, not a shortened one.
claims.why: _append_budget_round appends a round with _budget_turn for each seated adapter, thus recording the round.

claims.text: Round 2 prompts are built from these, not from the in-memory replies: a turn the secret floor refused is a receipt on disk, and re-feeding the raw reply would smuggle the refused bytes into another vendor's prompt.
claims.why: The docstring claims round 2 prompts are built from the chain, but the actual prompt construction (_round_body) is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Read this round's turns back FROM THE CHAIN.
claims.why: _chained reads from load_transcript(store) and filters by record type 'turn' and round number, which is reading from the chain (store).

claims.text: A blown wall clock is NOT handled here: the next iteration's top-of-round check records a budget_exhausted turn per participant first. Breaking early would shorten the council silently.
claims.why: The comment explains that a wall clock blow is not handled in the current iteration; the next iteration's top check will handle it. The code does not break early on wall clock within the round; it only checks at the top of the next round.

observations.what: The trusted lane check raises ValueError with a repair message, but the condition is not shown; it may reject localhost endpoints incorrectly if the endpoint is not actually off-machine.
The floor_check is called with evidence paths and files, but the exact semantics of 'per path, per file' and whether it scans the assembled prompt are not verifiable from this chunk.
The timeout detection relies on the presence of 'error' key in the box; the format of box is not pinned, so a vendor error might be misclassified.
The token ceiling check uses count_tokens and evidence.text_tokens, but the accuracy of these counts relative to vendor tokenizers is unverified.
The outcome update logic for 'refused' sets floor_rule only if not already set, which is correct; however, if a later refused turn has a different reason, it is ignored.

The participant_records are built from outcomes, but if the loop breaks due to 'no_voice' before all actors have been updated, actors who never spoke may retain 'seated' outcome instead of 'unavailable' or 'refused'.
The chain verification and transcript head are called, but their implementations are not in this chunk; the correctness of chain_intact and chain_head is uncheckable.
